data:
What constitutes a social movement? Why and how do social movements emerge? Who joins
social movements and why? What strategies do they use? How do social movements differ?
Which resources are essential for social movements? Why are some successful, and some are
not? These are some of the questions that the course intends to address.
Emphasis will be not only on the processes and career of the movements but also on the
conditions and contexts that give rise to collective mobilization. The students will be encouraged
to ultimately reflect on more general questions about the nature of political power, resources,
conflict, and legitimacy, as well as, the relationship between human agency, social structure, and
historical change.
